1.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called 2 be an apostle, separated 2 tha gospel of God,
(Which he had promised afore by his prophets in tha holy scriptures,)
Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of tha seed of David according 2 tha flesh;
N declared 2 be tha Son of God wit power, according 2 tha spirit of holiness, by tha resurrection from tha dead:
By whom we have received grace N apostleship, 4 obedience 2 tha faith among all nations, 4 his name:
Among whom r y’all also tha called of Jesus Christ:
2 all dat be in Rome, beloved of God, called 2 be saints: Grace 2 u N peace from God our Father, N tha Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ 4 u all, dat ur faith is spoken of throughout tha whole world.
4 God is my witness, whom I serve wit my spirit in tha gospel of his Son, dat without ceasing I make mention of u always in my prayers;
Makin request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by tha will of God 2 come 2 u.
4 I long 2 see u, dat I may impart 2 u some spiritual gift, 2 tha end y’all may be established;
Dat is, dat I may be comforted together wit u by tha mutual faith both of u N me.
Now I would not have u ignorant, brothers, dat oftentimes I purposed 2 come 2 u, (but was let until now,) dat I might have some fruit among u also, even as among other Gentiles.
I am debtor both 2 tha Greeks, N 2 tha Barbarians; both 2 tha wise, N 2 tha unwise.
So, as much as in me is, I am ready 2 preach tha gospel 2 u dat r at Rome also.
4 I am not ashamed of tha gospel of Christ: 4 it is tha power of God 2 salvation 2 every one dat believes; 2 tha Jew first, N also 2 tha Greek.
4 in it is tha righteousness of God revealed from faith 2 faith: as it is written, tha just shall live by faith.
4 tha wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness N unrighteousness of men, who hold tha truth in unrighteousness;
Because dat which may be known of God is manifest in ’em; 4 God has showed it 2 ’em.
4 tha invisible things of him from tha creation of tha world r clearly seen, bein understood by tha things dat r made, even his eternal power N Godhead; so dat dey r without excuse:
Because dat, when dey knew God, dey glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, N their foolish heart was darkened.
Professing themselves 2 be wise, dey became fools,
N changed tha glory of tha uncorruptible God in2 an image made like 2 corruptible man, N 2 birds, N fourfooted beasts, N creeping things.
So God also gave ’em up 2 uncleanness through tha lusts of their own hearts, 2 dishonour their own bodies between themselves:
Who changed tha truth of God in2 a lie, N worshipped N served tha creature more than tha Creator, who is blessed 4 ever. Amen.
4 dis cause God gave ’em up 2 vile affections: 4 even their women did change tha natural use in2 dat which is against nature:

N likewise also tha men, leavin tha natural use of tha woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men wit men workin dat which is unseemly, N receivin in themselves dat recompence of their error which was meet.
N even as dey did not like 2 retain God in their knowledge, God gave ’em over 2 a reprobate mind, 2 do dose things which r not convenient;
Bein filled wit all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient 2 parents,
Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:
Who knowin tha judgment of God, dat dey which commit such things r worthy of death, not only do tha same, but have pleasure in ’em dat do ’em.

2.text: Therefore u r inexcusable, O man, whoever u r dat judge: 4 in which u judge another, u condemnest urself; 4 u dat judge do tha same things.
But we r sure dat tha judgment of God is according 2 truth against ’em which commit such things.
N think u dis, O man, dat judge ’em which do such things, N do tha same, dat u will escape tha judgment of God?
Or despisest u tha riches of his goodness N forbearance N longsuffering; not knowin dat tha goodness of God leads u 2 repentance?
But after ur hardness N impenitent heart treasurest up 2 urself wrath against tha day of wrath N revelation of tha righteous judgment of God;
Who will render 2 every man according 2 his deeds:
2 ’em who by patient continuance in well doin seek 4 glory N honour N immortality, eternal life:
But 2 ’em dat r contentious, N do not obey tha truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation N wrath,
Tribulation N anguish, upon every soul of man dat does evil, of tha Jew first, N also of tha Gentile;
But glory, honour, N peace, 2 every man dat works good, 2 tha Jew first, N also 2 tha Gentile:
4 there is no respect of persons wit God.
4 as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: N as many as have sinned in tha law shall be judged by tha law;
(4 not tha hearers of tha law r just before God, but tha doers of tha law shall be justified.
4 when tha Gentiles, which have not tha law, do by nature tha things contained in tha law, dese, havin not tha law, r a law 2 themselves:
Which show tha work of tha law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearin witness, N their thoughts tha mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)
In tha day when God shall judge tha secrets of men by Jesus Christ according 2 my gospel.
Look, u r called a Jew, N restest in tha law, N make ur boast of God,
N know his will, N approvest tha things dat r more excellent, bein instructed out of tha law;
N art confident dat u urself art a guide of tha blind, a light of ’em which r in darkness,
An instructor of tha foolish, a teacher of babes, which have tha form of knowledge N of tha truth in tha law.
u therefore which teach another, teach u not urself? u dat preachest a man should not steal, do u steal?
u dat sayest a man should not commit adultery, do u commit adultery? u dat abhorrest idols, do u commit sacrilege?
u dat make ur boast of tha law, through breaking tha law dishonourest u God?
4 tha name of God is blasphemed among tha Gentiles through u, as it is written.
4 circumcision for real profits, if u keep tha law: but if u be a breaker of tha law, ur circumcision is made uncircumcision.
Therefore if tha uncircumcision keep tha righteousness of tha law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted 4 circumcision?
N shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil tha law, judge u, who by tha letter N circumcision do transgress tha law?
4 he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is dat circumcision, which is outward in tha flesh:
But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; N circumcision is dat of tha heart, in tha spirit, N not in tha letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

3.text: What advantage then has tha Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?
Much every way: chiefly, because dat 2 ’em were committed tha oracles of God.
4 what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make tha faith of God without effect?
God forbid: yeah, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, dat u might be justified in ur sayings, N might overcome when u r judged.
But if our unrighteousness commend tha righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who takes vengeance? (I speak as a man)
God forbid: 4 then how shall God judge tha world?
4 if tha truth of God has more abounded through my lie 2 his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
N not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, N as some affirm dat we say,) Let us do evil, dat good may come? whose damnation is just.
What then? r we better than dey? No, in no wise: 4 we have before proved both Jews N Gentiles, dat dey r all under sin;
As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:
There is none dat understands, there is none dat seeks after God.
Dey r all gone out of tha way, dey r together become unprofitable; there is none dat does good, no, not one.
Their throat is an open sepulchre; wit their tongues dey have used deceit; tha poison of asps is under their lips:
Whose mouth is full of cursing N bitterness:
Their feet r swift 2 shed blood:
Destruction N misery r in their ways:
N tha way of peace have dey not known:
There is no fear of God before their eyes.
Now we know dat what things soever tha law says, it says 2 ’em who r under tha law: dat every mouth may be stopped, N all tha world may become guilty before God.
Therefore by tha deeds of tha law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: 4 by tha law is tha knowledge of sin.
But now tha righteousness of God without tha law is manifested, bein witnessed by tha law N tha prophets;
Even tha righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ 2 all N upon all ’em dat believe: 4 there is no difference:
4 all have sinned, N come short of tha glory of God;
Bein justified freely by his grace through tha redemption dat is in Christ Jesus:
Whom God has set forth 2 be a propitiation through faith in his blood, 2 declare his righteousness 4 tha remission of sins dat r past, through tha forbearance of God;
2 declare, I say, at dis time his righteousness: dat he might be just, N tha justifier of him which believes in Jesus.
Where is boastin then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? no: but by tha law of faith.
Therefore we conclude dat a man is justified by faith without tha deeds of tha law.
Is he tha God of tha Jews only? is he not also of tha Gentiles? Yes, of tha Gentiles also:
Seein it is one God, which shall justify tha circumcision by faith, N uncircumcision through faith.
Do we then make void tha law through faith? God forbid: yeah, we establish tha law.

4.text: What shall we say then dat Abraham our father, as pertaining 2 tha flesh, has found?
4 if Abraham were justified by works, he has whereof 2 glory; but not before God.
4 what says tha scripture? Abraham believed God, N it was counted 2 him 4 righteousness.
Now 2 him dat works is tha reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.
But 2 him dat works not, but believes on him dat justifieth tha ungodly, his faith is counted 4 righteousness.
Even as David also describeth tha blessedness of tha man, 2 whom God imputeth righteousness without works,
Sayin, Blessed r dey whose iniquities r forgiven, N whose sins r covered.
Blessed is tha man 2 whom tha Lord will not impute sin.
Comes dis blessedness then upon tha circumcision only, or upon tha uncircumcision also? 4 we say dat faith was reckoned 2 Abraham 4 righteousness.
How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

N he received tha sign of circumcision, a seal of tha righteousness of tha faith which he had yet bein uncircumcised: dat he might be tha father of all ’em dat believe, though dey don’t be circumcised; dat righteousness might be imputed 2 ’em also:
N tha father of circumcision 2 ’em who r not of tha circumcision only, but who also walk in tha steps of dat faith of our father Abraham, which he had bein yet uncircumcised.
4 tha promise, dat he should be tha heir of tha world, was not 2 Abraham, or 2 his seed, through tha law, but through tha righteousness of faith.
4 if dey which r of tha law be heirs, faith is made void, N tha promise made of none effect:
Because tha law works wrath: 4 where no law is, there is no transgression.

Therefore it is of faith, dat it might be by grace; 2 tha end tha promise might be sure 2 all tha seed; not 2 dat only which is of tha law, but 2 dat also which is of tha faith of Abraham; who is tha father of us all,
(As it is written, I have made u a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth tha dead, N calls dose things which don’t be as though dey were.
Who against hope believed in hope, dat he might become tha father of many nations; according 2 dat which was spoken, So shall ur seed be.
N bein not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet tha deadness of Sara’s womb:
He staggered not at tha promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, givin glory 2 God;
N bein fully persuaded dat, what he had promised, he was able also 2 perform.
N therefore it was imputed 2 him 4 righteousness.
Now it was not written 4 his sake alone, dat it was imputed 2 him;
But 4 us also, 2 whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him dat raised up Jesus our Lord from tha dead;
Who was delivered 4 our offences, N was raised again 4 our justification.

5.text: Therefore bein justified by faith, we have peace wit God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
By whom also we have access by faith in2 dis grace in which we stand, N rejoice in hope of tha glory of God.
N not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowin dat tribulation works patience;
N patience, experience; N experience, hope:
N hope makes not ashamed; because tha love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by tha Holy Ghost which is given 2 us.
4 when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died 4 tha ungodly.
4 scarcely 4 a righteous man will one die: yet maybe 4 a good man some would even dare 2 die.
But God commendeth his love toward us, in dat, while we were yet sinners, Christ died 4 us.
Much more then, bein now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him.
4 if, when we were opps, we were reconciled 2 God by tha death of his Son, much more, bein reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.
N not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received tha atonement.
So, as by one man sin entered in2 tha world, N death by sin; N so death passed upon all men, 4 dat all have sinned:
(4 until tha law sin was in tha world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law.
Nevertheless death reigned from Adam 2 Moses, even over ’em dat had not sinned after tha similitude of Adam’s transgression, who is tha figure of him dat was 2 come.

But not as tha offence, so also is tha free gift. 4 if through tha offence of one many be dead, much more tha grace of God, N tha gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, has abounded 2 many.
N not as it was by one dat sinned, so is tha gift: 4 tha judgment was by one 2 condemnation, but tha free gift is of many offences 2 justification.
4 if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more dey which receive abundance of grace N of tha gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.)
Therefore as by tha offence of one judgment came upon all men 2 condemnation; even so by tha righteousness of one tha free gift came upon all men 2 justification of life.
4 as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by tha obedience of one shall many be made righteous.
Moreover tha law entered, dat tha offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound:
Dat as sin has reigned 2 death, even so might grace reign through righteousness 2 eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

6.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, dat grace may abound?
God forbid. How shall we, dat r dead 2 sin, live any longer in it?
Know y’all not, dat so many of us as were baptized in2 Jesus Christ were baptized in2 his death?
Therefore we r buried wit him by baptism in2 death: dat like as Christ was raised up from tha dead by tha glory of tha Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
4 if we have been planted together in tha likeness of his death, we shall be also in tha likeness of his resurrection:
Knowin dis, dat our old man is crucified wit him, dat tha body of sin might be destroyed, dat from now on we should not serve sin.
4 he dat is dead is freed from sin.
Now if we be dead wit Christ, we believe dat we shall also live wit him:
Knowin dat Christ bein raised from tha dead dies no more; death has no more dominion over him.
4 in dat he died, he died 2 sin once: but in dat he lives, he lives 2 God.
Likewise reckon y’all also y’all 2 be dead indeed 2 sin, but alive 2 God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Don’t let sin therefore reign in ur mortal body, dat y’all should obey it in tha lusts of it.
Neither yield y’all ur members as instruments of unrighteousness 2 sin: but yield y’all 2 God, as dose dat r alive from tha dead, N ur members as instruments of righteousness 2 God.
4 sin shall not have dominion over u: 4 y’all r not under tha law, but under grace.
What then? shall we sin, because we r not under tha law, but under grace? God forbid.
Know y’all not, dat 2 whom y’all yield y’all servants 2 obey, his servants y’all r 2 whom y’all obey; whether of sin 2 death, or of obedience 2 righteousness?
But God be thanked, dat y’all were tha servants of sin, but y’all have obeyed from tha heart dat form of doctrine which was delivered u.
Bein then made free from sin, y’all became tha servants of righteousness.

I speak after tha manner of men because of tha infirmity of ur flesh: 4 as y’all have yielded ur members servants 2 uncleanness N 2 iniquity 2 iniquity; even so now yield ur members servants 2 righteousness 2 holiness.
4 when y’all were tha servants of sin, y’all were free from righteousness.
What fruit had y’all then in dose things whereof y’all r now ashamed? 4 tha end of dose things is death.
But now bein made free from sin, N become servants 2 God, y’all have ur fruit 2 holiness, N tha end everlasting life.
4 tha wages of sin is death; but tha gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

7.text: Know y’all not, brothers, (4 I speak 2 ’em dat know tha law,) how dat tha law has dominion over a man as long as he lives?
4 tha woman which has an husband is bound by tha law 2 her husband so long as he lives; but if tha husband be dead, she is loosed from tha law of her husband.

So then if, while her husband lives, she be married 2 another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if her husband be dead, she is free from dat law; so dat she is no adulteress, though she be married 2 another man.
So, my brothers, y’all also r become dead 2 tha law by tha body of Christ; dat y’all should be married 2 another, even 2 him who is raised from tha dead, dat we should bring forth fruit 2 God.
4 when we were in tha flesh, tha motions of sins, which were by tha law, did work in our members 2 bring forth fruit 2 death.
But now we r delivered from tha law, dat bein dead in which we were held; dat we should serve in newness of spirit, N not in tha oldness of tha letter.
What shall we say then? Is tha law sin? God forbid. no, I had not known sin, but by tha law: 4 I had not known lust, except tha law had said, u will not covet.
But sin, takin occasion by tha commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. 4 without tha law sin was dead.
4 I was alive without tha law once: but when tha commandment came, sin revived, N I died.
N tha commandment, which was ordained 2 life, I found 2 be 2 death.
4 sin, takin occasion by tha commandment, deceived me, N by it killed me.
So tha law is holy, N tha commandment holy, N just, N good.
Was then dat which is good made death 2 me? God forbid. But sin, dat it might appear sin, workin death in me by dat which is good; dat sin by tha commandment might become exceeding sinful.
4 we know dat tha law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.
4 dat which I do I allow not: 4 what I would, dat do I not; but what I hate, dat do I.
If then I do dat which I would not, I consent 2 tha law dat it is good.
Now then it is no more I dat do it, but sin dat lives in me.
4 I know dat in me (dat is, in my flesh,) lives no good thing: 4 2 will is present wit me; but how 2 perform dat which is good I find not.
4 tha good dat I would I do not: but tha evil which I would not, dat I do.
Now if I do dat I would not, it is no more I dat do it, but sin dat lives in me.
I find then a law, dat, when I would do good, evil is present wit me.
4 I delight in tha law of God after tha inward man:
But I see another law in my members, warring against tha law of my mind, N bringin me in2 captivity 2 tha law of sin which is in my members.
O wretched man dat I am! who shall deliver me from tha body of dis death?
I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then wit tha mind I myself serve tha law of God; but wit tha flesh tha law of sin.

8.text: There is therefore now no condemnation 2 ’em which r in Christ Jesus, who walk not after tha flesh, but after tha Spirit.
4 tha law of tha Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from tha law of sin N death.
4 what tha law could not do, in dat it was weak through tha flesh, God sending his own Son in tha likeness of sinful flesh, N 4 sin, condemned sin in tha flesh:
Dat tha righteousness of tha law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after tha flesh, but after tha Spirit.
4 dey dat r after tha flesh do mind tha things of tha flesh; but dey dat r after tha Spirit tha things of tha Spirit.
4 2 be carnally minded is death; but 2 be spiritually minded is life N peace.
Because tha carnal mind is enmity against God: 4 it is not subject 2 tha law of God, neither indeed can be.
So then dey dat r in tha flesh cannot please God.
But y’all r not in tha flesh, but in tha Spirit, if so be dat tha Spirit of God live in u. Now if any man have not tha Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
N if Christ be in u, tha body is dead because of sin; but tha Spirit is life because of righteousness.
But if tha Spirit of him dat raised up Jesus from tha dead live in u, he dat raised up Christ from tha dead shall also quicken ur mortal bodies by his Spirit dat lives in u.
Therefore, brothers, we r debtors, not 2 tha flesh, 2 live after tha flesh.
4 if y’all live after tha flesh, y’all shall die: but if y’all through tha Spirit do mortify tha deeds of tha body, y’all shall live.
4 as many as r led by tha Spirit of God, dey r tha sons of God.
4 y’all have not received tha spirit of bondage again 2 fear; but y’all have received tha Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.
Tha Spirit itself bears witness wit our spirit, dat we r tha children of God:
N if children, then heirs; heirs of God, N joint-heirs wit Christ; if so be dat we suffer wit him, dat we may be also glorified together.
4 I reckon dat tha sufferings of dis present time r not worthy 2 be compared wit tha glory which shall be revealed in us.
4 tha earnest expectation of tha creature waits 4 tha manifestation of tha sons of God.
4 tha creature was made subject 2 vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who has subjected tha same in hope,
Because tha creature itself also shall be delivered from tha bondage of corruption in2 tha glorious liberty of tha children of God.
4 we know dat tha whole creation groaneth N labors in pain together until now.
N not only dey, but ourselves also, which have tha firstfruits of tha Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waitin 4 tha adoption, 2 wit, tha redemption of our body.
4 we r saved by hope: but hope dat is seen is not hope: 4 what a man sees, why does he yet hope 4?
But if we hope 4 dat we see not, then do we wit patience wait 4 it.
Likewise tha Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: 4 we know not what we should pray 4 as we ought: but tha Spirit itself makes intercession 4 us wit groanings which cannot be uttered.
N he dat searches tha hearts knows what is tha mind of tha Spirit, because he makes intercession 4 tha saints according 2 tha will of God.
N we know dat all things work together 4 good 2 ’em dat love God, 2 ’em who r tha called according 2 his purpose.
4 whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate 2 be conformed 2 tha image of his Son, dat he might be tha firstborn among many brothers.
Moreover whom he did predestinate, ’em he also called: N whom he called, ’em he also justified: N whom he justified, ’em he also glorified.
What shall we then say 2 dese things? If God be 4 us, who can be against us?
He dat spared not his own Son, but delivered him up 4 us all, how shall he not wit him also freely give us all things?
Who shall lay any thing 2 tha charge of God’s elect? It is God dat justifieth.
Who is he dat condemneth? It is Christ dat died, yeah rather, dat is risen again, who is even at tha right hand of God, who also makes intercession 4 us.
Who shall separate us from tha love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
As it is written, 4 ur sake we r killed all tha day long; we r accounted as sheep 4 tha slaughter.
No, in all dese things we r more than conquerors through him dat loved us.
4 I am persuaded, dat neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things 2 come,
Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able 2 separate us from tha love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

9.text: I say tha truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearin me witness in tha Holy Ghost,
Dat I have great heaviness N continual sorrow in my heart.
4 I could wish dat myself were accursed from Christ 4 my brothers, my kinsmen according 2 tha flesh:
Who r Israelites; 2 whom pertains tha adoption, N tha glory, N tha covenants, N tha givin of tha law, N tha service of God, N tha promises;
Whose r tha fathers, N of whom as concerning tha flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed 4 ever. Amen.
Not as though tha word of God has taken none effect. 4 dey r not all Israel, which r of Israel:
Neither, because dey r tha seed of Abraham, r dey all children: but, In Isaac shall ur seed be called.
Dat is, dey which r tha children of tha flesh, dese r not tha children of God: but tha children of tha promise r counted 4 tha seed.
4 dis is tha word of promise, At dis time will I come, N Sara shall have a son.
N not only dis; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac;
(4 tha children bein not yet born, neither havin done any good or evil, dat tha purpose of God according 2 election might stand, not of works, but of him dat calls;)
It was said 2 her, tha elder shall serve tha younger.
As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness wit God? God forbid.
4 he says 2 Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, N I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
So then it is not of him dat willeth, nor of him dat runs, but of God dat shows mercy.
4 tha scripture says 2 Pharaoh, Even 4 dis same purpose have I raised u up, dat I might show my power in u, N dat my name might be declared throughout all tha earth.
Therefore has he mercy on whom he will have mercy, N whom he will he hardeneth.
u will say then 2 me, Why does he yet find fault? 4 who has resisted his will?
No but, O man, who r u dat repliest against God? Shall tha thing formed say 2 him dat formed it, Why have u made me like dis?
Has not tha potter power over tha clay, of tha same lump 2 make one vessel 2 honour, N another 2 dishonour?
What if God, willin 2 show his wrath, N 2 make his power known, endured wit much longsuffering tha vessels of wrath fitted 2 destruction:
N dat he might make known tha riches of his glory on tha vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared 2 glory,
Even us, whom he has called, not of tha Jews only, but also of tha Gentiles?
As he says also in Osee, I will call ’em my people, which were not my people; N her beloved, which was not beloved.
N it will happen, dat in tha place where it was said 2 ’em, y’all r not my people; there shall dey be called tha children of tha livin God.
Esaias also cries concerning Israel, Though tha number of tha children of Israel be as tha sand of tha sea, a remnant shall be saved:
4 he will finish tha work, N cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will tha Lord make upon tha earth.
N as Esaias said before, Except tha Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, N been made like 2 Gomorrha.
What shall we say then? dat tha Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained 2 righteousness, even tha righteousness which is of faith.
But Israel, which followed after tha law of righteousness, has not attained 2 tha law of righteousness.
So? Because dey sought it not by faith, but as it were by tha works of tha law. 4 dey stumbled at dat stumblingstone;
As it is written, look, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone N rock of offence: N whoever believes on him shall not be ashamed.

10.text: Brothers, my heart’s desire N prayer 2 God 4 Israel is, dat dey might be saved.
4 I bear ’em record dat dey have a zeal of God, but not according 2 knowledge.
4 dey bein ignorant of God’s righteousness, N goin about 2 establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves 2 tha righteousness of God.
4 Christ is tha end of tha law 4 righteousness 2 every one dat believes.
4 Moses describeth tha righteousness which is of tha law, dat tha man which does dose things shall live by ’em.
But tha righteousness which is of faith speaks on dis wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend in2 heaven? (dat is, 2 bring Christ down from above:)
Or, Who shall descend in2 tha deep? (dat is, 2 bring up Christ again from tha dead.)
But what says it? tha word is nigh u, even in ur mouth, N in ur heart: dat is, tha word of faith, which we preach;
Dat if u will confess wit ur mouth tha Lord Jesus, N will believe in thine heart dat God has raised him from tha dead, u will be saved.
4 wit tha heart man believes 2 righteousness; N wit tha mouth confession is made 2 salvation.
4 tha scripture says, whoever believes on him shall not be ashamed.
4 there is no difference between tha Jew N tha Greek: 4 tha same Lord over all is rich 2 all dat call upon him.
4 whoever shall call upon tha name of tha Lord shall be saved.
How then shall dey call on him in whom dey have not believed? N how shall dey believe in him of whom dey have not heard? N how shall dey hear without a preacher?
N how shall dey preach, except dey be sent? as it is written, How beautiful r tha feet of ’em dat preach tha gospel of peace, N bring glad tidings of good things!
But dey have not all obeyed tha gospel. 4 Esaias says, Lord, who has believed our report?
So then faith comes by hearin, N hearin by tha word of God.
But I say, Have dey not heard? Yes for real, their sound went in2 all tha earth, N their words 2 tha ends of tha world.
But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses says, I will provoke u 2 jealousy by ’em dat r no people, N by a foolish nation I will anger u.
But Esaias is very bold, N says, I was found of ’em dat sought me not; I was made manifest 2 ’em dat asked not after me.
But 2 Israel he says, All day long I have stretched forth my hands 2 a disobedient N gainsaying people.

11.text: I say then, has God cast away his people? God forbid. 4 I also am an Israelite, of tha seed of Abraham, of tha tribe of Benjamin.
God has not cast away his people which he foreknew. know y’all not what tha scripture says of Elias? how he makes intercession 2 God against Israel, sayin,
Lord, dey have killed ur prophets, N digged down thine altars; N I am left alone, N dey seek my life.
But what says tha answer of God 2 him? I have reserved 2 myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed tha knee 2 tha image of Baal.
Even so then at dis present time also there is a remnant according 2 tha election of grace.
N if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.
What then? Israel has not obtained dat which he seeks 4; but tha election has obtained it, N tha rest were blinded
(According as it is written, God has given ’em tha spirit of slumber, eyes dat dey should not see, N ears dat dey should not hear;) 2 dis day.
N David says, Let their table be made a snare, N a trap, N a stumblingblock, N a recompence 2 ’em:
Let their eyes be darkened, dat dey may not see, N bow down their back alway.
I say then, Have dey stumbled dat dey should fall? God forbid: but rather through their fall salvation is come 2 tha Gentiles, 4 2 provoke ’em 2 jealousy.
Now if tha fall of ’em be tha riches of tha world, N tha diminishing of ’em tha riches of tha Gentiles; how much more their fulness?
4 I speak 2 u Gentiles, since as I am tha apostle of tha Gentiles, I magnify mine office:
If by any means I may provoke 2 emulation ’em which r my flesh, N might save some of ’em.
4 if tha castin away of ’em be tha reconciling of tha world, what shall tha receivin of ’em be, but life from tha dead?
4 if tha firstfruit be holy, tha lump is also holy: N if tha root be holy, so r tha branches.
N if some of tha branches be broken off, N u, bein a wild olive tree, were graffed in among ’em, N wit ’em partakest of tha root N fatness of tha olive tree;
Boast not against tha branches. But if u boast, u bear not tha root, but tha root u.
u will say then, tha branches were broken off, dat I might be graffed in.
Well; because of unbelief dey were broken off, N u stand by faith. don’t be highminded, but fear:
4 if God spared not tha natural branches, pay attention lest he also spare not u.
Look therefore tha goodness N severity of God: on ’em which fell, severity; but toward u, goodness, if u continue in his goodness: otherwise u also will be cut off.
N dey also, if dey abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: 4 God is able 2 graff ’em in again.

4 if u were cut out of tha olive tree which is wild by nature, N were graffed contrary 2 nature in2 a good olive tree: how much more shall dese, which be tha natural branches, be graffed in2 their own olive tree?

4 I would not, brothers, dat y’all should be ignorant of dis mystery, lest y’all should be wise in ur own conceits; dat blindness in part is happened 2 Israel, until tha fulness of tha Gentiles be come in.
N so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion tha Deliverer, N shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:
4 dis is my covenant 2 ’em, when I shall take away their sins.
As concerning tha gospel, dey r opps 4 ur sakes: but as touching tha election, dey r beloved 4 tha fathers’ sakes.
4 tha gifts N callin of God r without repentance.
4 as y’all in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief:
Even so have dese also now not believed, dat through ur mercy dey also may obtain mercy.
4 God has concluded ’em all in unbelief, dat he might have mercy upon all.
O tha depth of tha riches both of tha wisdom N knowledge of God! how unsearchable r his judgments, N his ways past finding out!
4 who has known tha mind of tha Lord? or who has been his counsellor?
Or who has first given 2 him, N it will be recompensed 2 him again?
4 of him, N through him, N 2 him, r all things: 2 whom be glory 4 ever. Amen.

12.text: I beg u therefore, brothers, by tha mercies of God, dat y’all present ur bodies a livin sacrifice, holy, acceptable 2 God, which is ur reasonable service.
N don’t be conformed 2 dis world: but be y’all transformed by tha renewing of ur mind, dat y’all may prove what is dat good, N acceptable, N perfect, will of God.

4 I say, through tha grace given 2 me, 2 every man dat is among u, not 2 think of himself more highly than he ought 2 think; but 2 think soberly, according as God has dealt 2 every man tha measure of faith.
4 as we have many members in one body, N all members have not tha same office:
So we, bein many, r one body in Christ, N every one members one of another.
Havin then gifts differing according 2 tha grace dat is given 2 us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according 2 tha proportion of faith;
Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he dat teaches, on teachin;
Or he dat exhorteth, on exhortation: he dat gives, let him do it wit simplicity; he dat rules, wit diligence; he dat shows mercy, wit cheerfulness.
Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor dat which is evil; cleave 2 dat which is good.
Be kindly affectioned one 2 another wit brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;
Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; servin tha Lord;
Rejoicin in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;
Distributing 2 tha necessity of saints; given 2 hospitality.
Bless ’em which persecute u: bless, N curse not.
Rejoice wit ’em dat do rejoice, N weep wit ’em dat weep.
Be of tha same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend 2 men of low estate. don’t be wise in ur own conceits.
Recompense 2 no man evil 4 evil. Provide things honest in tha sight of all men.
If it be possible, as much as lies in u, live peaceably wit all men.
Dearly beloved, avenge not y’all, but rather give place 2 wrath: 4 it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says tha Lord.
Therefore if thine opp hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: 4 in so doin u will heap coals of fire on his head.
Don’t be overcome of evil, but overcome evil wit good.

13.text: Let every soul be subject 2 tha higher powers. 4 there is no power but of God: tha powers dat be r ordained of God.
Whoever therefore resisteth tha power, resisteth tha ordinance of God: N dey dat resist shall receive 2 themselves damnation.
4 rulers r not a terror 2 good works, but 2 tha evil. will u then not be afraid of tha power? do dat which is good, N u will have praise of tha same:
4 he is tha minister of God 2 u 4 good. But if u do dat which is evil, be afraid; 4 he bears not tha sword in vain: 4 he is tha minister of God, a revenger 2 execute wrath upon him dat does evil.
So y’all must needs be subject, not only 4 wrath, but also 4 conscience sake.
4 4 dis cause pay y’all tribute also: 4 dey r God’s ministers, attending continually upon dis very thing.
Render therefore 2 all their dues: tribute 2 whom tribute is due; custom 2 whom custom; fear 2 whom fear; honour 2 whom honour.
Owe no man any thing, but 2 love one another: 4 he dat loves another has fulfilled tha law.

4 dis, u will not commit adultery, u will not kill, u will not steal, u will not bear false witness, u will not covet; N if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in dis sayin, namely, u will love ur neighbour as urself.
Love works no ill 2 his neighbour: therefore love is tha fulfilling of tha law.
N dat, knowin tha time, dat now it is high time 2 awake out of sleep: 4 now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.
Tha night is far spent, tha day is at hand: let us therefore cast off tha works of darkness, N let us put on tha armour of light.
Let us walk honestly, as in tha day; not in rioting N drunkenness, not in chambering N wantonness, not in strife N envying.
But put y’all on tha Lord Jesus Christ, N make not provision 4 tha flesh, 2 fulfil tha lusts of it.

14.text: Him dat is weak in tha faith receive y’all, but not 2 doubtful disputations.
4 one believes dat he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eats herbs.
Don’t let him dat eats despise him dat eats not; N don’t let him which eats not judge him dat eats: 4 God has received him.
Who r u dat judge another man’s servant? 2 his own master he stands or falls. yeah, he shall be holden up: 4 God is able 2 make him stand.
One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.

He dat regards tha day, regards it 2 tha Lord; N he dat regards not tha day, 2 tha Lord he does not regard it. He dat eats, eats 2 tha Lord, 4 he gives God thanks; N he dat eats not, 2 tha Lord he eats not, N gives God thanks.
4 none of us lives 2 himself, N no man dies 2 himself.
4 whether we live, we live 2 tha Lord; N whether we die, we die 2 tha Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we r tha Lord’s.
4 2 dis end Christ both died, N rose, N revived, dat he might be Lord both of tha dead N livin.
But why do u judge ur brother? or why do u set at nothing ur brother? 4 we shall all stand before tha judgment seat of Christ.
4 it is written, As I live, says tha Lord, every knee shall bow 2 me, N every tongue shall confess 2 God.
So then every one of us shall give account of himself 2 God.
Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge dis rather, dat no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion 2 fall in his brother’s way.
I know, N am persuaded by tha Lord Jesus, dat there is nothing unclean of itself: but 2 him dat esteemeth any thing 2 be unclean, 2 him it is unclean.
But if ur brother be grieved wit ur food, now walk u not charitably. Destroy not him wit ur food, 4 whom Christ died.
Don’t let then ur good be evil spoken of:
4 tha kingdom of God is not food N drink; but righteousness, N peace, N joy in tha Holy Ghost.
4 he dat in dese things serves Christ is acceptable 2 God, N approved of men.
Let us therefore follow after tha things which make 4 peace, N things wherewith one may edify another.
4 food destroy not tha work of God. All things indeed r pure; but it is evil 4 dat man who eats wit offence.
It is good neither 2 eat flesh, nor 2 drink wine, nor any thing whereby ur brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak.
Have u faith? have it 2 urself before God. Happy is he dat condemneth not himself in dat thing which he alloweth.
N he dat doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eats not of faith: 4 whatever is not of faith is sin.

15.text: We then dat r strong ought 2 bear tha infirmities of tha weak, N not 2 please ourselves.
Let every one of us please his neighbour 4 his good 2 edification.
4 even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, tha reproaches of ’em dat reproached u fell on me.
4 whatever things were written aforetime were written 4 our learning, dat we through patience N comfort of tha scriptures might have hope.
Now tha God of patience N consolation grant u 2 be likeminded one toward another according 2 Christ Jesus:
Dat y’all may wit one mind N one mouth glorify God, even tha Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So receive y’all one another, as Christ also received us 2 tha glory of God.
Now I say dat Jesus Christ was a minister of tha circumcision 4 tha truth of God, 2 confirm tha promises made 2 tha fathers:
N dat tha Gentiles might glorify God 4 his mercy; as it is written, 4 dis cause I will confess 2 u among tha Gentiles, N sing 2 ur name.
N again he says, Rejoice, y’all Gentiles, wit his people.
N again, Praise tha Lord, all y’all Gentiles; N laud him, all y’all people.
N again, Esaias says, There shall be a root of Jesse, N he dat shall rise 2 reign over tha Gentiles; in him shall tha Gentiles trust.
Now tha God of hope fill u wit all joy N peace in believin, dat y’all may abound in hope, through tha power of tha Holy Ghost.
N I myself also am persuaded of u, my brothers, dat y’all also r full of goodness, filled wit all knowledge, able also 2 admonish one another.
Nevertheless, brothers, I have written tha more boldly 2 u in some sort, as puttin u in mind, because of tha grace dat is given 2 me of God,
Dat I should be tha minister of Jesus Christ 2 tha Gentiles, ministering tha gospel of God, dat tha offering up of tha Gentiles might be acceptable, bein sanctified by tha Holy Ghost.
I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ in dose things which pertain 2 God.
4 I will not dare 2 speak of any of dose things which Christ has not wrought by me, 2 make tha Gentiles obedient, by word N deed,
Through mighty signs N wonders, by tha power of tha Spirit of God; so dat from Jerusalem, N round about 2 Illyricum, I have fully preached tha gospel of Christ.
Yeah, so have I strived 2 preach tha gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man’s foundation:
But as it is written, 2 whom he was not spoken of, dey shall see: N dey dat have not heard shall understand.
4 which cause also I have been much hindered from comin 2 u.
But now havin no more place in dese parts, N havin a great desire dese many years 2 come 2 u;
Whensoever I take my journey in2 Spain, I will come 2 u: 4 I trust 2 see u in my journey, N 2 be brought on my way thitherward by u, if first I be somewhat filled wit ur company.
But now I go 2 Jerusalem 2 minister 2 tha saints.
4 it has pleased ’em of Macedonia N Achaia 2 make a certain contribution 4 tha poor saints which r at Jerusalem.
It has pleased ’em for real; N their debtors dey r. 4 if tha Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also 2 minister 2 ’em in carnal things.
When therefore I have performed dis, N have sealed 2 ’em dis fruit, I will come by u in2 Spain.
N I am sure dat, when I come 2 u, I shall come in tha fulness of tha blessing of tha gospel of Christ.
Now I beg u, brothers, 4 tha Lord Jesus Christ’s sake, N 4 tha love of tha Spirit, dat y’all strive together wit me in ur prayers 2 God 4 me;
Dat I may be delivered from ’em dat do not believe in Judaea; N dat my service which I have 4 Jerusalem may be accepted of tha saints;
Dat I may come 2 u wit joy by tha will of God, N may wit u be refreshed.
Now tha God of peace be wit u all. Amen.

16.text: I commend 2 u Phebe our sister, which is a servant of tha church which is at Cenchrea:
Dat y’all receive her in tha Lord, as becomes saints, N dat y’all assist her in whatever business she has need of u: 4 she has been a succourer of many, N of myself also.
Greet Priscilla N Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:
Who have 4 my life laid down their own necks: 2 whom not only I give thanks, but also all tha churches of tha Gentiles.
Likewise greet tha church dat is in their house. greet my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is tha firstfruits of Achaia 2 Christ.
Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.
Greet Andronicus N Junia, my kinsmen, N my fellowprisoners, who r of note among tha apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
Greet Amplias my beloved in tha Lord.
Greet Urbane, our helper in Christ, N Stachys my beloved.
Greet Apelles approved in Christ. greet ’em which r of Aristobulus’ household.
Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet ’em dat be of tha household of Narcissus, which r in tha Lord.
Greet Tryphena N Tryphosa, who labour in tha Lord. greet tha beloved Persis, which laboured much in tha Lord.
Greet Rufus chosen in tha Lord, N his mother N mine.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, N tha brothers which r wit ’em.
Greet Philologus, N Julia, Nereus, N his sister, N Olympas, N all tha saints which r wit ’em.
Greet one another wit an holy kiss. tha churches of Christ greet u.
Now I beg u, brothers, mark ’em which cause divisions N offences contrary 2 tha doctrine which y’all have learned; N avoid ’em.
4 dey dat r such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; N by good words N fair speeches deceive tha hearts of tha simple.
4 ur obedience is come abroad 2 all men. I am glad therefore on ur behalf: but yet I would have u wise 2 dat which is good, N simple concerning evil.
N tha God of peace shall bruise Satan under ur feet shortly. tha grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be wit u. Amen.
Timotheus my workfellow, N Lucius, N Jason, N Sosipater, my kinsmen, greet u.
I Tertius, who wrote dis epistle, greet u in tha Lord.
Gaius mine host, N of tha whole church, saluteth u. Erastus tha chamberlain of tha city saluteth u, N Quartus a brother.
Tha grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be wit u all. Amen.
Now 2 him dat is of power 2 stablish u according 2 my gospel, N tha preachin of Jesus Christ, according 2 tha revelation of tha mystery, which was kept secret since tha world began,
But now is made manifest, N by tha scriptures of tha prophets, according 2 tha commandment of tha everlasting God, made known 2 all nations 4 tha obedience of faith:
2 God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ 4 ever. Amen.
